questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the context.**

She was so tired that she _________ asleep immediately.
questions.solution:
‘Fall’ is the verb generally used with ‘asleep’. The given sentence is in **simple past tense**. So, we need to use the appropriate past tense verb of fall i.e. **fell**.

Hence, **option 3 is correct.**

Note: Observe that ‘felt’ is the past tense of ‘feel’ and not ‘fall’.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

I helped my sister ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__make her project__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• When a person helps another person in performing a task, the given pattern is followed:
 
• Subject + *help/helps/helped *+ object + infinitive form of verb
 
• **For eg: **

 *My mother helped me **bake **a cake for my sister. (infinitive form)

 Clara helped him **climb **the stairs. (infinitive form)*
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase to fill the blank will be **make her project, **where 'make' is the infinitive form of the verb.
 
• Hence, **option 3 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the context.**

The door opened with a ________ sound.
questions.solution:
**Tinkling** is to make a light ringing sound.

**Whistling** is a sound made when one whistles.

**Murmur** is to say something in a soft, quiet voice.

**Creaking** refers to the sound a door makes while opening it or the sound wooden floor makes when one steps on it. So, **creaking **is the correct word in the given context.

Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the context.**

He _________ the letter and put it in his bag.
questions.solution:
To solve this question, we must look at the logic of the context.

It does not make sense to **turn** or **bend **a letter before putting it in a bag and one cannot **double **the letter unless he/she is a magician.

So, he must have ‘**folded**’ the letter, since that is the most logical word to fit the context.

Hence, **option 3 is correct.**

questions.question: **From the below, select the sentence that is grammatically correct and meaningful in the given context.**

options.text: Tractors are used by their fields to plough farmers.
By farmers their tractors are used fields to plough.
Their fields to plough tractors are used by farmers.
Tractors are used by farmers to plough their fields.

questions.solution:
Farmers use tractors to plough their fields to cultivate crops. This is the intended meaning of the given options. All the options are in passive voice.

To understand the given question better, let’s convert “Farmers use tractors to plough their fields” to passive voice.

This would result in *"Tractors are used by farmers to plough their fields."* Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

It can be observed that the other options convey the meaning 'to plough farmers and tractors', which is not logical or meaningful and hence incorrect.

questions.question:
**Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.**

The boys asked the teacher if they were going to have a holiday the next day.

options.text: The boys asked the teacher, “Were they going to have a holiday the next day?”
The boys asked the teacher, “Are we going to have a holiday tomorrow?”
The boys asked the teacher, “Do we have a holiday tomorrow?”
The boys told the teacher, “We going to have a holiday tomorrow.”

questions.solution:
‘The boys asked’ indicates** simple past tense.** The word ‘if’ indicates that a question was asked.

While converting indirect to direct, the past tense has to be changed to equivalent present tense and third person pronoun to second or first person. Therefore, ‘the next day’ changes to ‘tomorrow’ in the direct form.

Hence, the correct direct form of the given sentence is expressed in **option 2.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.**

A partner in crime
questions.solution:
**Accomplice **is a person who helps another commit a crime, i.e. a partner in crime. Assistant, associate or colleague are all individuals who help or work with us in a business or organisation, not in a crime.

Hence, **option 1 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the word which is opposite in meaning to the word in capitals.**

SUSPEND
questions.solution:
**Suspend **is to stop/prevent something from continuing. So, **continue **is the word which is opposite in meaning to suspend.

Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

For generations, the tradition of equating the visitors with God has been followed by our village.

options.text: For generations, the visitors have followed the tradition of equating our village with God.
For generations, our village has been following the tradition of equating the visitors with God.
For generations, our village has followed the tradition of equating the visitors with God.
For generations, our village was following the tradition of equating the visitors with God.

questions.solution:
**Passive form:** object + verb (past participle) + by + subject

**Active form: **Subject + appropriate verb + object

Here, it can be seen that ‘our village’ is the subject, ‘the tradition of equating the visitors with God’ is the object and ‘had been followed’ is the verb.

‘Had been followed’ is changed to ‘has followed’ in the active voice. ‘has been following’ is grammatically wrong. 

Hence, the correct answer is **option 3.**

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Shobhit said, “Mohit often helps me with Mathematics.”

options.text: Shobhit said Mohit often helps me with Mathematics.
Shobhit said that Mohit often helping him with Mathematics.
Shobhit said that Mohit was often helping him with Mathematics.
Shobhit said that Mohit often helped him with Mathematics.

questions.solution:
‘Shobhit **said’ **points out that it was said in the **past**. Hence, the sentence in quotes should be changed to past tense in the indirect form.

**helps → helped**

Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question: What is unique about the town of Shani Singnapur?

options.text: Many pilgrims come to visit the town from faraway places.
The town has a temple to the deity Shani.
There are no doors to the houses in the whole town.
The people of the town have great faith in lord Shani.

questions.solution:
The word ‘unique’ is used to mean that there is only one of its kind. The passage clearly implies that houses with no doors are seen only in Shani Singnapur.

Hence, **option 3 is correct.**

questions.question: Why don’t people of Shani Shingnapur lock their homes?

options.text: They cannot buy locks in the market.
They have great faith in lord Shani.
People in the town are honest.
They ask the neighbours to keep a watch.

questions.solution:
The passage states *‘such is their staunch faith in Lord Shani that they even travel out of town for days without asking their neighbours to keep vigil’.*

Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true according to the passage?

options.text: Initially the temple of Shani used to be small.
Mustard oil keeps pouring on the idol of Lord Shani continuously.
Lord Shani’s idol is mounted on a platform.
The idol of Lord Shani is covered from three sides.

questions.solution:
In the given passage, each of the statements above is mentioned at various points in the passage except the statement in **option 4. **It is mentioned nowhere in the passage that the idol of Lord Shani is covered from three sides.

**Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: How do people in Shani Shingnapur maintain their privacy?

options.text: They use door frames for entrances.
Plywood is used at the bottom half of entrance.
Latches are installed in the entrance.

questions.solution:
The passage states that for the citizens of the town, "*curtains can provide some sense of privacy".*

Hence, **option 4 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Match words in column A with their meanings in column B.**

 
 

 
 
**Column A**

 
 
 
**Column B**

 
 
 

 
 
a. surge

 
 
 
1. example

 
 
 

 
 
b. vigil

 
 
 
2. increase

 
 
 

 
 
c. instance

 
 
 
3. watch
questions.solution:
The word **surge **means a sudden large **increase**, typically a temporary one. Hence **a **matches with **2.**

The word **vigil **means a period of keeping awake during the time usually spent asleep, especially to keep **watch**. Hence **b **matches with **3.**

The word **instance **means an **example **or single occurrence of something. Hence **c **matches with 1.

The only option that mentions all of these combinations is **option 2.**

questions.question:
**Given below are six sentences with the first and the last in their correct order; however, the remaining four are jumbled. Pick the option that gives the correct order.**

Sentence 1. Emilia and her family lived on the island of Sebesi—one of the largest islands in the Sunda Strait— located near the Anak Krakatau volcano.

P. Sebesi island is one of several areas that was badly hit by the tsunami, which was triggered after volcanic activity at Anak Krakatau caused undersea landslides.

Q. Vast waves engulfed coastal towns on the islands of Sumatra and Java leaving at least 430 dead and more than 150 missing.

R. It destroyed hundreds of buildings, sweeping away cars and uprooting trees in several popular tourist destinations on Saturday.

S. At least 16,000 people still remain displaced and rescue workers are struggling to reach remote areas of the country that have been hit by the tsunami.

Sentence 6. Emelia is one of 90 people who have been hospitalised at the Bob Bazar hospital in the nearby town of Kalianda.
questions.solution:
**P should be the first sentence **as it gives the introduction about the tsunami. Q, R and S describe the effects of the tsunami.

The sixth sentence states about people being hospitalized. So, the fourth and fifth sentences must be about the people (Q and S).

The word ‘still’ in sentence S hints that S comes after Q. R is therefore, the third sentence.

The correct order should be **PRQS**.

Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question:

Health authorities should foster good practice by diseminating information.
questions.solution:
The correct spelling is ‘**di__ss__eminating**’ which means to spread or circulate information.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.**

Ragini’s parents do not like Mohit, but he keeps meeting her **__on and off__.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. __Occasionally__**

 
• ‘**On and off**’ means ‘**once in a while**’, which means not regularly. **Occasionally **also means the same.
 
• It does not refer to whether he meets her secretly or openly, hence options 1 and 2 are incorrect.

Hence, **option 3) **conveys the correct meaning of the underlined phrase.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment of the sentence given below that contains a grammatical error.**

Young people in Britain eats more snacks than people of the same age in other European countries.

options.text: than people of the same age

questions.solution:
**Subject-verb agreement error:**

Here the subject is ‘Young people of Britain’, which is plural. A plural verb should be used with a plural subject.

‘eat’ is plural verb and ‘eats’ is a singular verb.

Hence, the error is in the part mentioned in **option 2. **

The correct sentence should be: 

*Young people in Britain **eat **more snacks than people of the same age in other European countries.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the context.**

The suffering of children at the shelter home _________ our sympathy.
questions.solution:
• **Arouse:** awaken or cause a feeling or emotion
 
• **Raise:** increase the amount, level or strength
 
• **Arose:** past tense of arise, which means occur or originate
 
• **Create:** to make something

 

We can see that the word **aroused **most meaningfully fits the blank. This is also because the word 'sympathy' is often preceded by the word 'arouse', as opposed to the other options.

Hence, **option 1 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

All the members happily paid the one-time subscription for the ‘Swacchta Abhiyan’ in the colony.

options.text: The one-time subscription for the Swacchta Abhiyan in the colony has been paid happily by all the members.
The one-time subscription for the Swacchta Abhiyan in the colony is being paid happily by all the members.
The one-time subscription for all the members in the colony was paid happily by the Swacchta Abhiyan.
The one-time subscription for the Swacchta Abhiyan in the colony was paid happily by all the members.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The one-time subscription for the Swacchta Abhiyan in the colony was paid happily by all the members.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Active Voice. As per the given question we have to change it into Passive Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence as follows:
 
 
• Subject + V2+ Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case)+ was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is '**All the members**'.​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is '**the one-time subscription for the ‘Swacchta Abhiyan’ in the colony**'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• And 'paid' will be changed into 'was paid'. 
 
• Lastly, the 'by' preposition will be added. 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4.

 ​

Correct Sentence:__ *The one-time subscription for the Swacchta Abhiyan in the colony was paid happily by all the members.*
